sanskrit: uta śalya vijānīhi hanta bhūyo bravīmi te yad apy anyo 'bravīd vākyaṃ bāhlīkānāṃ vikutsitam
english: Know this too, O Śalya — come, I will tell you yet more — the words another man spoke in condemnation of the Bāhlīkas.

sanskrit: satī purā hṛtā kā cid āraṭṭā kila dasyubhiḥ adharmataś copayātā sā tān abhyaśapat tataḥ
english: Long ago a certain chaste woman of Āraṭṭa was carried off by robbers, they say, and wrongfully ravished; thereupon she laid this curse upon them:

sanskrit: bālāṃ bandhumatīṃ yan mām adharmeṇopagacchatha tasmān nāryo bhaviṣyanti bandhakyo vai kuleṣu vaḥ na caivāsmāt pramokṣyadhvaṃ ghorāt pāpān narādhamāḥ
english: "Because you have approached me unlawfully — a young girl with kinsmen still living — the women of your houses shall become harlots, and never shall you be freed from this dreadful sin, O basest of men."

sanskrit: kuravaḥ sahapāñcālāḥ śālvā matsyāḥ sanaimiṣāḥ kosalāḥ kāśayo 'ṅgāś ca kaliṅgā magadhās tathā
english: The Kurus together with the Pāñcālas, the Śālvas, the Matsyas and the Naimiṣas, the Kosalas, the Kāśis, the Aṅgas, the Kaliṅgas, and the Magadhas as well —

sanskrit: cedayaś ca mahābhāgā dharmaṃ jānanti śāśvatam nānādeśeṣu santaś ca prāyo bāhyā layād ṛte
english: and the illustrious Cedis — these know the eternal law; and good men in many lands, for the most part, keep to it, save those who have lapsed.

sanskrit: ā matsyebhyaḥ kurupāñcāladeśyā; ā naimiṣāc cedayo ye viśiṣṭāḥ dharmaṃ purāṇam upajīvanti santo; madrān ṛte pañcanadāṃś ca jihmān
english: From the lands of the Kurus and Pāñcālas down to the Matsyas, and from the Naimiṣa region the excellent Cedis — these good folk live by the ancient law, all save the Madras and the crooked people of the Five Rivers.

sanskrit: evaṃ vidvan dharmakathāṃś ca rājaṃs; tūṣṇīṃbhūto jaḍavac chalya bhūyāḥ tvaṃ tasya goptā ca janasya rājā; ṣaḍbhāgahartā śubhaduṣkṛtasya
english: Knowing such discourses on the law, O king, you ought to stay silent like a dolt, Śalya; for you are the protector and ruler of that people, and you take a sixth part of their merit and their sin alike.

sanskrit: atha vā duṣkṛtasya tvaṃ hartā teṣām arakṣitā rakṣitā puṇyabhāg rājā prajānāṃ tvaṃ tv apuṇyabhāk
english: Or rather, you take only a share of their evildoing, since you fail to protect them; the king who guards his subjects has a share in their merit, but you have a share only in their demerit.

sanskrit: pūjyamāne purā dharme sarvadeśeṣu śāśvate dharmaṃ pāñcanadaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhig ity āha pitāmahaḥ
english: In olden times, when the eternal law was honored in every land, the Grandsire, beholding the ways of the Five Rivers, cried out, "Shame!"

sanskrit: vrātyānāṃ dāśamīyānāṃ kṛte 'py aśubhakarmaṇām iti pāñcanadaṃ dharmam avamene pitāmahaḥ svadharmastheṣu varṇeṣu so 'py etaṃ nābhipūjayet
english: On account of those outcaste, low-bred men of unclean deeds, the Grandsire scorned the practice of the Five Rivers; even when the four orders abide each in its own duty, he would not honor that custom.

sanskrit: uta śalya vijānīhi hanta bhūyo bravīmi te kalmāṣapādaḥ sarasi nimajjan rākṣaso 'bravīt
english: Know this too, O Śalya — come, I will tell you yet more — what the Rākṣasa Kalmāṣapāda said as he was sinking in a lake:

sanskrit: kṣatriyasya malaṃ bhaikṣaṃ brāhmaṇasyānṛtaṃ malam malaṃ pṛthivyā bāhlīkāḥ strīṇāṃ madrastriyo malam
english: "Begging is the defilement of a Kṣatriya, falsehood the defilement of a Brāhmaṇa; the Bāhlīkas are the defilement of the earth, and the Madra women the defilement of all womankind."

sanskrit: nimajjamānam uddhṛtya kaś cid rājā niśācaram apṛcchat tena cākhyātaṃ proktavān yan nibodha tat
english: A certain king, having pulled the night-prowler up as he was sinking, questioned him; and what that demon then declared, hear it now.

sanskrit: mānuṣāṇāṃ malaṃ mlecchā mlecchānāṃ mauṣṭikā malam mauṣṭikānāṃ malaṃ śaṇḍāḥ śaṇḍānāṃ rājayājakāḥ
english: "The Mlecchas are the defilement of mankind, the Mauṣṭikas the defilement of the Mlecchas; the Śaṇḍas are the defilement of the Mauṣṭikas, and the priests of kings the defilement of the Śaṇḍas."

sanskrit: rājayājakayājyānāṃ madrakāṇāṃ ca yan malam tad bhaved vai tava malaṃ yady asmān na vimuñcasi
english: "And the defilement of those Madrakas who employ kings' priests as their sacrificers — that very defilement shall be yours, if you do not let me go."

sanskrit: iti rakṣopasṛṣṭeṣu viṣavīryahateṣu ca rākṣasaṃ bheṣajaṃ proktaṃ saṃsiddhaṃ vacanottaram
english: Thus, for those afflicted by a Rākṣasa or struck down by the power of poison, this demon's utterance was declared a proven remedy, a charm against such ills.

sanskrit: brāhmaṃ pāñcālāḥ kauraveyāḥ svadharmaḥ; satyaṃ matsyāḥ śūrasenāś ca yajñaḥ prācyā dāsā vṛṣalā dākṣiṇātyāḥ; stenā bāhlīkāḥ saṃkarā vai surāṣṭrāḥ
english: The Pāñcālas keep the Vedic law, the Kauravas their own duty; the Matsyas embody truth, the Śūrasenas sacrifice; the Easterners are slaves, the Southerners low men, the Bāhlīkas are thieves, and the Surāṣṭras born of mixed castes.

sanskrit: kṛtaghnatā paravittāpahāraḥ; surāpānaṃ gurudārāvamarśaḥ yeṣāṃ dharmas tān prati nāsty adharma; āraṭṭakān pāñcanadān dhig astu
english: Ingratitude, the seizing of another's wealth, the drinking of liquor, and the violating of a teacher's wife — for those whose law is this there is no such thing as sin; shame upon the Āraṭṭas, the people of the Five Rivers!

sanskrit: ā pāñcālebhyaḥ kuravo naimiṣāś ca; matsyāś caivāpy atha jānanti dharmam kaliṅgakāś cāṅgakā māgadhāś ca; śiṣṭān dharmān upajīvanti vṛddhāḥ
english: From the Kurus to the Pāñcālas, the Naimiṣas, and the Matsyas too — these know the law; and the Kaliṅgas, the Aṅgas, the Magadhas, and the elders live by the ordinances of the wise.

sanskrit: prācīṃ diśaṃ śritā devā jātavedaḥpurogamāḥ dakṣiṇāṃ pitaro guptāṃ yamena śubhakarmaṇā
english: The eastern quarter is held by the gods, with Agni the knower-of-beings at their head; the southern, guarded by Yama of holy deeds, belongs to the ancestral fathers.

sanskrit: pratīcīṃ varuṇaḥ pāti pālayann asurān balī udīcīṃ bhagavān somo brahmaṇyo brāhmaṇaiḥ saha
english: The western quarter the mighty Varuṇa guards, watching over the Asuras; the northern is the lord Soma's, friend of the Veda, dwelling there together with the Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: rakṣaḥpiśācān himavān guhyakān gandhamādanaḥ dhruvaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni viṣṇur lokāñ janārdanaḥ
english: Himavat presides over the Rākṣasas and Piśācas, Gandhamādana over the Guhyakas; Dhruva watches over all beings, and Viṣṇu Janārdana over the worlds.

sanskrit: iṅgitajñāś ca magadhāḥ prekṣitajñāś ca kosalāḥ ardhoktāḥ kurupāñcālāḥ śālvāḥ kṛtsnānuśāsanāḥ pārvatīyāś ca viṣamā yathaiva girayas tathā
english: The Magadhas understand a hint, the Kosalas a mere glance; the Kurus and Pāñcālas grasp a half-spoken word, the Śālvas need the whole command; but the hillmen are as rugged as the very mountains.

sanskrit: sarvajñā yavanā rājañ śūrāś caiva viśeṣataḥ mlecchāḥ svasaṃjñāniyatā nānukta itaro janaḥ
english: The Yavanas, O king, are all-knowing and brave above all; the Mlecchas follow only their own usages; but other folk understand nothing unless it is plainly told.

sanskrit: pratirabdhās tu bāhlīkā na ca ke cana madrakāḥ sa tvam etādṛśaḥ śalya nottaraṃ vaktum arhasi
english: The Bāhlīkas stand condemned, and no Madrakas escape it either; and you, Śalya, being of such a stock, have no right to make reply.

sanskrit: etaj jñātvā joṣam āssva pratīpaṃ mā sma vai kṛthāḥ sa tvāṃ pūrvam ahaṃ hatvā haniṣye keśavārjunau
english: Knowing this, hold your peace and do not work against me; else I will slay you first, and then slay Keśava and Arjuna both.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca āturāṇāṃ parityāgaḥ svadārasutavikrayaḥ aṅgeṣu vartate karṇa yeṣām adhipatir bhavān
english: Śalya said: The abandoning of the sick and the selling of one's own wives and sons go on among the Aṅgas, Karṇa — those people whose overlord you are.

sanskrit: rathātirathasaṃkhyāyāṃ yat tvā bhīṣmas tadābravīt tān viditvātmano doṣān nirmanyur bhava mā krudhaḥ
english: What Bhīṣma once said of you in the reckoning of chariot-warriors and master-warriors — knowing these faults of your own, lay aside your wrath, and be not angry.

sanskrit: sarvatra brāhmaṇāḥ santi santi sarvatra kṣatriyāḥ vaiśyāḥ śūdrās tathā karṇa striyaḥ sādhvyaś ca suvratāḥ
english: Everywhere there are Brāhmaṇas, everywhere Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras too, O Karṇa, and virtuous women faithful to their vows.

sanskrit: ramante copahāsena puruṣāḥ puruṣaiḥ saha anyonyam avatakṣanto deśe deśe samaithunāḥ
english: And men everywhere take their pleasure in jesting, one with another, cutting at each other in raillery; in every land there are those given to such sport.

sanskrit: paravācyeṣu nipuṇaḥ sarvo bhavati sarvadā ātmavācyaṃ na jānīte jānann api vimuhyati
english: Everyone is forever skilled at finding fault with others, but knows nothing of his own faults — or, knowing them, is blind.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca karṇo 'pi nottaraṃ prāha śalyo 'py abhimukhaḥ parān punaḥ prahasya rādheyaḥ punar yāhīty acodayat
english: Saṃjaya said: Karṇa made no answer, and Śalya turned to face the foe; then Rādheya, laughing once more, urged him on again, saying, "Drive on!"

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ parānīkabhidaṃ vyūham apratimaṃ paraiḥ samīkṣya karṇaḥ pārthānāṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnābhirakṣitam
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Karṇa, surveying the matchless battle-array of the Pārthas, that breaker of hostile lines guarded by Dhṛṣṭadyumna,

sanskrit: prayayau rathaghoṣeṇa siṃhanādaraveṇa ca vāditrāṇāṃ ca ninadaiḥ kampayann iva medinīm
english: advanced with the thunder of his chariot, with lion-roars, and with the blare of instruments, as though making the earth itself tremble.

sanskrit: vepamāna iva krodhād yuddhaśauṇḍaḥ paraṃtapaḥ pativyūhya mahātejā yathāvad bharatarṣabha
english: Quivering, as it were, with rage, that battle-mad scorcher of foes, the mighty-splendored one, drew up his ranks in due order, O bull of the Bharatas,

sanskrit: vyadhamat pāṇḍavīṃ senām āsurīṃ maghavān iva yudhiṣṭhiraṃ cābhibhavann asapavyaṃ cakāra ha
english: and scattered the Pāṇḍava host as Maghavat scatters the army of the Asuras; bearing down upon Yudhiṣṭhira, he turned him to his left.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kathaṃ saṃjaya rādheyaḥ pratyavyūhata pāṇḍavān dhṛṣṭadyumnamukhān vīrān bhīmasenābhirakṣitān
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: How, Saṃjaya, did Rādheya array himself against the Pāṇḍavas — those heroes led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna and guarded by Bhīmasena?

sanskrit: ke ca prapakṣau pakṣau vā mama sainyasya saṃjaya pravibhajya yathānyāyaṃ kathaṃ vā samavasthitāḥ
english: And who, Saṃjaya, were the flanks and the wings of my army, and how were they posted, drawn up each in its proper place?

sanskrit: kathaṃ pāṇḍusutāś cāpi pratyavyūhanta māmakān kathaṃ caitan mahāyuddhaṃ prāvartata sudāruṇam
english: And how too did the sons of Pāṇḍu array themselves against my men, and how did that great and most terrible battle begin?

sanskrit: kva ca bībhatsur abhavad yat karṇo 'yād yudhiṣṭhiram ko hy arjunasya sāṃnidhye śakto 'bhyetuṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: And where was Bībhatsu when Karṇa advanced upon Yudhiṣṭhira? For who, with Arjuna near at hand, could dare to close with Yudhiṣṭhira?

sanskrit: sarvabhūtāni yo hy ekaḥ khāṇḍave jitavān purā kas tam anyatra rādheyāt pratiyudhyej jijīviṣuḥ
english: He who once, single-handed, vanquished all beings at the Khāṇḍava — who, save Rādheya, would fight against him and still wish to live?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śṛṇu vyūhasya racanām arjunaś ca yathā gataḥ paridāya nṛpaṃ tebhyaḥ saṃgrāmaś cābhavad yathā
english: Saṃjaya said: Hear the ordering of the array, and how Arjuna went forth, having committed the king to others' care, and how the battle then came to pass.

sanskrit: kṛpaḥ śāradvato rājan māgadhaś ca tarasvinaḥ sātvataḥ kṛtavarmā ca dakṣiṇaṃ pakṣam āśritāḥ
english: Kṛpa, son of Śaradvat, O king, and the swift Māgadha, and Kṛtavarman of the Sātvata line held the right wing.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ prapakṣe śakunir ulūkaś ca mahārathaḥ sādibhir vimalaprāsais tavānīkam arakṣatām
english: On their flank Śakuni and the great chariot-warrior Ulūka, with horsemen bearing bright lances, guarded your host.

sanskrit: gāndhāribhir asaṃbhrāntaiḥ pārvatīyaiś ca durjayaiḥ śalabhānām iva vrātaiḥ piśācair iva durdṛśaiḥ
english: with unshaken men of Gāndhāra and unconquerable hillmen, who came on in swarms like locusts and were as dreadful to look upon as Piśācas.

sanskrit: catustriṃśat sahasrāṇi rathānām anivartinām saṃśaptakā yuddhaśauṇḍā vāmaṃ pārśvam apālayan
english: Thirty-four thousand chariots that never turned back — the battle-mad Saṃśaptakas — guarded the left flank.

sanskrit: samuccitās tava sutaiḥ kṛṣṇārjunajighāṃsavaḥ teṣāṃ prapakṣaḥ kāmbojāḥ śakāś ca yavanaiḥ saha
english: Mustered by your sons and eager to slay Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, they had as their wing the Kāmbojas, the Śakas, and the Yavanas.

sanskrit: nideśāt sūtaputrasya sarathāḥ sāśvapattayaḥ āhvayanto 'rjunaṃ tasthuḥ keśavaṃ ca mahābalam
english: At the command of the Sūta's son, with their chariots, horse, and foot, they took their stand, challenging Arjuna and the mighty Keśava.

sanskrit: madhyesenāmukhaṃ karṇo vyavātiṣṭhata daṃśitaḥ citravarmāṅgadaḥ sragvī pālayan dhvajinīmukham
english: In the center, at the army's head, Karṇa took his post, mailed, with gleaming armor and armlets and garlands, guarding the front of the host.

sanskrit: rakṣyamāṇaḥ susaṃrabdhaiḥ putraiḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ vāhinīpramukhaṃ vīraḥ saṃprakarṣann aśobhata
english: Guarded by your fiercely wrathful sons, that best of weapon-bearers, the hero, shone as he led on the vanguard of the army.

sanskrit: ayoratnir mahābāhuḥ sūryavaiśvānaradyutiḥ mahādvipaskandhagataḥ piṅgalaḥ priyadarśanaḥ duḥśāsano vṛtaḥ sainyaiḥ sthito vyūhasya pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: Iron-fisted, mighty-armed, with the radiance of the sun and of fire, tawny-eyed and fair to behold, mounted on the shoulders of a great elephant, Duḥśāsana, surrounded by troops, stood at the rear of the array.

sanskrit: tam anvayān mahārāja svayaṃ duryodhano nṛpaḥ citrāśvaiś citrasaṃnāhaiḥ sodaryair abhirakṣitaḥ
english: Behind him, O great king, came King Duryodhana himself, guarded by his own brothers with their gaily caparisoned horses and bright armor.

sanskrit: rakṣyamāṇo mahāvīryaiḥ sahitair madrakekayaiḥ aśobhata mahārāja devair iva śatakratuḥ
english: Guarded by the mighty Madrakas and Kekayas joined together, he shone, O great king, like Indra of the hundred sacrifices amid the gods.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā kurūṇāṃ ca ye pravīrā mahārathāḥ nityamattāś ca mātaṅgāḥ śūrair mlecchair adhiṣṭhitāḥ anvayus tad rathānīkaṃ kṣaranta iva toyadāḥ
english: Aśvatthāman and the foremost great chariot-warriors of the Kurus, and ever-rutting elephants ridden by valiant Mlecchas, followed that array of chariots like rain-shedding clouds.

sanskrit: te dhvajair vaijayantībhir jvaladbhiḥ paramāyudhaiḥ sādibhiś cāsthitā rejur drumavanta ivācalāḥ
english: With their banners and pennons, with blazing peerless weapons, and manned by their riders, they shone like mountains clothed in forest.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ padātināgānāṃ pādarakṣāḥ sahasraśaḥ paṭṭiśāsidharāḥ śūrā babhūvur anivartinaḥ
english: Footguards by the thousand — valiant men bearing pikes and swords, who never turned back — went at the feet of those elephants and foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: sādibhiḥ syandanair nāgair adhikaṃ samalaṃkṛtaiḥ sa vyūharājo vibabhau devāsuracamūpamaḥ
english: With its horsemen, chariots, and elephants richly adorned, that king of arrays shone forth like the host of gods and Asuras.

sanskrit: bārhaspatyaḥ suvihito nāyakena vipaścitā nṛtyatīva mahāvyūhaḥ pareṣām ādadhad bhayam
english: Disposed after the fashion of Bṛhaspati, well ordered by its wise commander, the great array seemed to dance, and struck terror into the foe.

sanskrit: tasya pakṣaprapakṣebhyo niṣpatanti yuyutsavaḥ pattyaśvarathamātaṅgāḥ prāvṛṣīva balāhakāḥ
english: From its wings and flanks the eager warriors poured forth — foot, horse, chariots, and elephants — like storm-clouds in the rainy season.

sanskrit: tataḥ senāmukhe karṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ dhanaṃjayam amitraghnam ekavīram uvāca ha
english: Then, beholding Karṇa at the army's head, King Yudhiṣṭhira spoke to Dhanaṃjaya, slayer of foes, the matchless hero:

sanskrit: paśyārjuna mahāvyūhaṃ karṇena vihitaṃ raṇe yuktaṃ pakṣaiḥ prapakṣaiś ca senānīkaṃ prakāśate
english: "Behold, Arjuna, the great array set in order by Karṇa for the battle; furnished with wings and flanks, the host stands resplendent."

sanskrit: tad etad vai samālokya pratyamitraṃ mahad balam yathā nābhibhavaty asmāṃs tathā nītir vidhīyatām
english: "Looking, then, upon this mighty hostile force, let such a plan be devised that it may not overwhelm us."

sanskrit: evam ukto 'rjuno rājñā prāñjalir nṛpam abravīt yathā bhavān āha tathā tat sarvaṃ na tad anyathā
english: Thus addressed by the king, Arjuna, with hands joined in reverence, said to him: "It is wholly as you say, and not otherwise."

sanskrit: yas tv asya vihito ghātas taṃ kariṣyāmi bhārata pradhānavadha evāsya vināśas taṃ karomy aham
english: "The destruction appointed for it I shall accomplish, O Bhārata; its ruin lies in the slaying of its chief, and that I will achieve."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca tasmāt tvam eva rādheyaṃ bhīmasenaḥ suyodhanam vṛṣasenaṃ ca nakulaḥ sahadevo 'pi saubalam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Therefore you yourself take Rādheya, Bhīmasena Suyodhana, Nakula Vṛṣasena, and Sahadeva the son of Subala;

sanskrit: duḥśāsanaṃ śatānīko hārdikyaṃ śinipuṃgavaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnas tathā drauṇiṃ svayaṃ yāsyāmy ahaṃ kṛpam
english: Śatānīka take Duḥśāsana, the bull of the Śini line take Hārdikya, Dhṛṣṭadyumna take Droṇa's son, and I myself will go against Kṛpa;

sanskrit: draupadeyā dhārtarāṣṭrāñ śiṣṭān saha śikhaṇḍinā te te ca tāṃs tān ahitān asmākaṃ ghnantu māmakāḥ
english: let the sons of Draupadī with Śikhaṇḍin take the remaining sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; and let each of my men slay each of those several enemies of ours.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ity ukto dharmarājena tathety uktvā dhanaṃjayaḥ vyādideśa svasainyāni svayaṃ cāgāc camūmukham
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus addressed by the King of Righteousness, Dhanaṃjaya answered, "So be it," and gave his orders to his own troops, and himself advanced to the army's front.

sanskrit: atha taṃ ratham āyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvātyadbhutadarśanam uvācādhirathiṃ śalyaḥ punas taṃ yuddhadurmadam
english: Then, seeing that chariot of wondrous aspect coming on, Śalya spoke once more to Karṇa, the son of Adhiratha, that man maddened for battle:

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa ratha āyāti śvetāśvaḥ kṛṣṇasārathiḥ nighnann amitrān kaunteyo yaṃ yaṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: "Here comes that very chariot, drawn by white horses and driven by Kṛṣṇa — the son of Kuntī, slaying his foes, after whom you have been asking again and again."

sanskrit: śrūyate tumulaḥ śabdo rathanemisvano mahān eṣa reṇuḥ samudbhūto divam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati
english: "A tumultuous din is heard, the loud rumble of chariot-wheels; this dust has risen up and stands veiling the very sky."

sanskrit: cakranemipraṇunnā ca kampate karṇa medinī pravāty eṣa mahāvāyur abhitas tava vāhinīm kravyādā vyāharanty ete mṛgāḥ kurvanti bhairavam
english: "Pounded by chariot-wheels the earth trembles, Karṇa; this great wind blows on every side of your host; and these flesh-eating beasts cry out, making a fearful clamor."

sanskrit: paśya karṇa mahāghoraṃ bhayadaṃ lomaharṣaṇam kabandhaṃ meghasaṃkāśaṃ bhānum āvṛtya saṃsthitam
english: "Behold, Karṇa, most dreadful, terrifying, and hair-raising, a headless trunk dark as a cloud, standing there veiling the sun."

sanskrit: paśya yūthair bahuvidhair mṛgāṇāṃ sarvatodiśam balibhir dṛptaśārdūlair ādityo 'bhinirīkṣyate
english: "Behold how the sun is stared at from every quarter by manifold herds of beasts and by mighty, arrogant tigers."

sanskrit: paśya kaṅkāṃś ca gṛdhrāṃś ca samavetān sahasraśaḥ sthitān abhimukhān ghorān anyonyam abhibhāṣataḥ
english: "Behold the herons and the vultures gathered by the thousand, standing fronting us, dreadful, calling out one to another."

sanskrit: sitāś cāśvāḥ samāyuktās tava karṇa mahārathe pradarāḥ prajvalanty ete dhvajaś caiva prakampate
english: "White are the horses yoked to your great chariot, Karṇa; these meteors blaze, and your banner too is trembling."

sanskrit: udīryato hayān paśya mahākāyān mahājavān plavamānān darśanīyān ākāśe garuḍān iva
english: "Behold his horses springing forward, huge of frame and swift, fair to see, as though flying through the sky like Garuḍas."

sanskrit: dhruvam eṣu nimitteṣu bhūmim āvṛtya pārthivāḥ svapsyanti nihatāḥ karṇa śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: "Surely, at these omens, the kings, slain in hundreds and in thousands, Karṇa, shall lie sleeping, covering the earth."

sanskrit: śaṅkhānāṃ tumulaḥ śabdaḥ śrūyate lomaharṣaṇaḥ ānakānāṃ ca rādheya mṛdaṅgānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: "A tumultuous, hair-raising sound is heard, Rādheya — of conch-shells and of war-drums and of tabors, on every side."

sanskrit: bāṇaśabdān bahuvidhān narāśvarathanisvanān jyātalatreṣuśabdāṃś ca śṛṇu karṇa mahātmanām
english: "Hear, Karṇa, the manifold twang of arrows, the din of men and horses and chariots, and the noise of bowstrings, hand-guards, and shafts of those great-souled warriors."
